answer: Admission is a locked cipher: each newcomer gets an encrypted token that opens only once several randomly drawn established agents each release a key-share, and a share is handed over only after that agent independently verifies the newcomer did real work. One operator spinning up clones cannot gather enough independent shares, so the network stays a guarded oasis admitting one real identity at a time, while a lantern of honest verifiers marks which shares are genuine. Flooding with fakes stalls because no single actor controls the scattered keys.
